title: Relevance profile - Section 138 NI Act (cheque dishonour)
description: Cross-act index of the provisions, definitions, procedure, evidence and disposal rules relevant to a Section 138 cheque-bounce case. References point into the canonical Akoma Ntoso files in this corpus; nothing is copied. Point-in-time aware: procedure/penal/evidence references resolve to the pre-2024 codes or the 2023 Sanhitas depending on the cause-of-action date.
ref_format: '<alias>:<eId>'. Resolve to the file at sources[alias].file, element eId; the logical AKN id is sources[alias].uri + '/eng@#' + eId (which equals the <FRBRuri> inside that file).
caveats: Section numbers were extracted from India Code reprint PDFs; verify against the official source before authoritative use.
'applies' indicates the cause-of-action window: 'always' (substantive/interpretive), 'pre-2024-07-01' (old codes), 'post-2024-07-01' (Sanhitas). Use act_alias_map to switch by date.
Landmark case law (e.g. Rangappa, Dashrath Rupsingh + 2015 amendment, Damodar S. Prabhu, Expeditious Trial 2021, Sanjabij Tari 2025) is not in this corpus and should be layered separately.

Constitution of India was re-converted from the India Code reprint PDF (Articles 1-395, best-effort). A few lettered articles and deep clause nesting are approximate; verify against the official source.

link_integrity.method: every ref '<alias>:<eId>' was verified to exist as an eId in sources[alias].file; unresolved refs were dropped, not shipped.
link_integrity.note: Constitution of India re-converted from the India Code PDF (Articles 1-395); constitution:art_21 and the other constitutional references now resolve.

provisions.note: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds; Explanation defines 'debt or other liability' as a legally enforceable debt.
Presumption in favour of the holder that the cheque was for discharge of a debt/liability.
Absence of reason to believe the cheque would be dishonoured is no defence.
Offences by companies; who is vicariously liable and the director's defence.
Cognizance only on complaint by the payee/HDC, within one month of cause of action (condonable); s.142(2) fixes territorial jurisdiction at the payee's bank branch.
Validation of transfer of pending cases after the 2015 jurisdiction amendment.
Power of court to try s.138 cases summarily (invokes the summary-trial provisions of the criminal procedure code).
Interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount.
Mode of service of summons on the accused.
Complainant's evidence may be given on affidavit.
Bank's slip/memo is prima facie evidence of dishonour.
Every offence under the Act is compoundable.
Appellate court may order deposit of min 20% of the fine/compensation pending appeal.
Includes a cheque in the electronic form and a truncated cheque (Explanation).
The complainant under s.138 must be the payee or the holder in due course.
Blank/incomplete cheques later filled in - a common s.138 defence issue.
Effect of material alteration of the instrument - a defence issue.
General presumptions (consideration, date, etc.) read with s.139.
Presentment of cheque to charge the drawer.
When a cheque is not duly presented and the drawer is damaged thereby.

provisions.role: right to life & personal liberty - fair & speedy trial
provisions.note: The constitutional anchor for expeditious disposal of s.138 complaints (In re Expeditious Trial of Cases under s.138 NI Act, 2021) and for scrutiny of default/sentence of imprisonment; guarantees a fair procedure established by law.

provisions.role: Supreme Court's power to do complete justice
provisions.note: Source of the compounding-cost guidelines (Damodar S. Prabhu v. Sayed Babalal, 2010) and of directions to settle/close s.138 cases (Meters and Instruments v. Kanchan Mehta, 2018; In re Expeditious Trial, 2021).
Together with s.482 CrPC / s.528 BNSS, the route to quash a s.138 complaint or challenge the proceedings; the writ power is independent of the inherent power.
Supervisory jurisdiction over the trial magistrate hearing the s.138 case; used to test interlocutory orders, transfers and delay.

provisions.role: law declared by Supreme Court is binding
provisions.note: Makes the s.138 case law (Rangappa, Dashrath Rupsingh, Damodar Prabhu, Expeditious Trial, etc.) binding on every court trying these cases.

provisions.role: special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court
provisions.note: The discretionary route by which s.138 matters reach the Supreme Court after the High Court.
Legislative competence for the NI Act: Entry 46 of List III (Concurrent) - 'bills of exchange, cheques, promissory notes and other like instruments'.

provisions.role: equal justice & free legal aid (Directive Principle)
provisions.note: Underlies referral of s.138 disputes to Lok Adalat / mediation and other access-to-justice measures; a Directive Principle, not directly enforceable.

provisions.role: protection in respect of conviction - ex-post-facto & self-incrimination
provisions.note: Art. 20(1)'s bar on retrospective penal/pecuniary liability informs the prospective-only application of the s.143A interim-compensation power (G.J. Raja v. Tejraj Surana, 2019); Art. 20(3) is raised where specimen signatures/handwriting are compelled.
Frames challenges to arbitrary procedure and supports the 'regulatory / compensatory offence' characterisation of s.138.
Only one class of persons may practise the profession of law - advocates. The complainant and the accused in a s.138 case are represented by advocates enrolled under this Act.
Every enrolled advocate's right, as of right, to practise in all courts - including the Magistrate trying a s.138 complaint. This is the source of the Advocate role.
The court may permit a person who is not an advocate to appear in a particular case - the basis on which a party in person, or a duly authorised agent, is heard in a s.138 matter.
Professional-misconduct control over the advocate appearing in the case, exercised by the State Bar Council on a complaint.

The police officer's duty to promptly obey and execute all orders and warrants lawfully issued by a competent authority and to apprehend persons - what the police act under when a s.138 court issues summons or warrants for a non-appearing accused. The Kerala Police Act operationalises this at the state level.
Penalty on a police officer who neglects or wilfully breaches a lawful order made by a competent authority - the accountability behind executing the court's process.

An officer sued for an act done under a Magistrate's warrant may plead the warrant and is entitled to judgment notwithstanding any defect of jurisdiction - protection for the officer who executes the court's process.

The general diary the station-house officer must keep - complaints and charges, persons arrested, complainants, offences and the witnesses examined - open to inspection by the Magistrate of the district.
Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property - the offence commonly filed alongside a s.138 complaint where the cheque was issued with no intention to pay.
Cheating (BNS). = IPC s.420. Often co-charged with a s.138 complaint.
A cheque is a valuable security; forging or materially altering it is a separate, graver offence than the s.138 dishonour.
Forgery of a valuable security (BNS). = IPC s.467.
Using as genuine a forged document - e.g. presenting a forged cheque.
Using a forged document/record as genuine (BNS). = IPC s.471.
The Payment and Settlement Systems Act analogue of s.138 - dishonour of an electronic funds transfer for insufficiency of funds. Increasingly relevant as clearing moves to CTS / electronic modes.

Public servant disobeying the law with intent to cause injury. In practice invoked to hold a police officer accountable - and thereby to compel action - where the officer knowingly disregards a lawful direction such as a warrant issued in a s.138 case. = IPC s.166.
Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury. Used to force the police to act on warrants where an officer knowingly disregards the court's lawful direction.
Intentional omission to apprehend by a public servant bound to apprehend - the offence where a police officer wilfully fails to execute a warrant or arrest a non-appearing s.138 accused. = IPC s.221.
Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of a public servant bound to apprehend - police wilfully not executing a warrant.
Public servant disobeying a direction under law, with intent to save a person from punishment - accountability where lawful process is not acted on. = IPC s.217.
Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save a person from punishment.

cheque.gloss: A bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and payable on demand; includes the truncated cheque and the electronic-image cheque.

negotiable instrument.gloss: A promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable to order or to bearer.

bill of exchange.gloss: A written order directing a person to pay a certain sum to, or to the order of, a person or the bearer.

promissory note.gloss: A written promise to pay a certain sum to, or to the order of, a person or the bearer.

banker.gloss: A person carrying on the business of banking; the drawee of a cheque.

negotiation.gloss: The transfer of an instrument so as to constitute the transferee its holder.

indorsement.gloss: Signing on an instrument (usually the back) for the purpose of negotiating it.

crossed cheque.gloss: A cheque marked so that it must be paid through a bank account, not across the counter.

maturity.gloss: The date on which an instrument falls due for payment.

drawer.gloss: The person who makes (draws) the cheque; the accused in a s.138 case.

drawee.gloss: The banker on whom the cheque is drawn and who is directed to pay.

payee.gloss: The person named in the instrument as the one to whom payment is to be made.

holder.gloss: The person entitled in their own name to possession of the instrument and to receive its amount.

holder in due course.gloss: A holder who took the instrument for value, in good faith and before maturity.

payment in due course.gloss: Payment made in accordance with the apparent tenor of the instrument, in good faith and without negligence.

company liability.gloss: Where the drawer is a company, the persons in charge of and responsible to it for the conduct of its business are also liable.

person in charge.gloss: The director or officer who, at the time of the offence, was in charge of and responsible to the company for its business - the test for vicarious liability.
aka: officer in charge of the company

defence not allowed.gloss: It is no defence in a s.138 prosecution that the drawer had no reason to believe the cheque would be dishonoured.

dishonour of cheque.gloss: The offence: a cheque given for a legally enforceable debt, returned unpaid for insufficiency of funds or because it exceeds the arrangement.

insufficiency of funds.gloss: The account not holding enough to honour the cheque - the trigger for the offence.

legally enforceable debt or liability.gloss: The debt or liability the cheque must discharge; by the Explanation and s.139, presumed to exist unless rebutted (Rangappa).

demand notice.gloss: The written notice the payee must give the drawer within 30 days of learning of dishonour, demanding payment of the cheque amount.

stop-payment.gloss: Instructing the bank not to pay; still a dishonour attracting s.138 where a legally enforceable debt exists.

presumption in favour of holder.gloss: The court shall presume the cheque was received for the discharge of a debt or liability - a reverse onus on the accused.

presumptions as to negotiable instrument.gloss: Presumptions of consideration, date, time of acceptance, transfer and the holder being a holder in due course.

rebuttal of presumption.gloss: The accused may rebut the s.139 presumption on the preponderance of probabilities, not beyond reasonable doubt.

evidence on affidavit.gloss: The complainant's evidence may be given on affidavit and read in any inquiry, trial or other proceeding.

bank's return memo.gloss: The banker's slip or memo of dishonour is prima facie evidence of the fact of dishonour.

bankers' books evidence.gloss: Certified copies of entries in a banker's books are admissible without producing the original books.

electronic record.gloss: The conditions for admitting electronic records as evidence - e.g., CTS cheque images and e-statements.

electronic signature.gloss: Authentication of an electronic record by an electronic technique specified in the Second Schedule.

complaint.gloss: A s.138 case begins on the payee's written complaint (not an FIR); the Magistrate examines the complainant on oath.

cognizance.gloss: The Magistrate taking judicial notice of the offence so as to set the case in motion.

issue of process.gloss: The Magistrate issuing summons (or a warrant) to secure the accused's attendance.

summons.gloss: The court's written order to a person to appear - the first step to bring in the accused.

mode of service of summons.gloss: In s.138, summons may be served by speed post or an approved courier and is deemed served even if the accused refuses it.

warrant.gloss: The court's written authority to arrest and produce a person who does not answer summons.

proclamation.gloss: A public notice requiring an absconding accused to appear - the step before attachment.

attachment.gloss: Attachment of an absconder's property to compel appearance.

summary trial.gloss: s.138 cases are tried summarily, with a simplified and faster procedure.

cognizance of offences.gloss: Who may complain, the one-month limitation, and the court that has territorial jurisdiction.

territorial jurisdiction.gloss: The case lies where the payee's bank branch (the collecting branch) is situated (post-2015 amendment).

revision.gloss: Calling for the record of a subordinate court to test the legality of an order - the usual route after a s.138 conviction.

quashing (inherent powers).gloss: The High Court's power to quash a complaint to prevent abuse of process or to secure the ends of justice.

deemed service of notice.gloss: Notice sent by registered post to the correct address is deemed served, even if returned unclaimed.

one-month limitation.gloss: The complaint must be filed within one month of the cause of action arising.

condonation of delay.gloss: The court may admit a complaint filed after time on sufficient cause being shown.

compounding.gloss: s.138 offences are compoundable - the parties may settle and bring the case to an end.

interim compensation.gloss: The court may order the drawer to pay up to 20% of the cheque amount as interim compensation.

appeal deposit.gloss: On appeal against conviction, the court may require a deposit of at least 20% of the fine or compensation.

probation.gloss: Release of an offender on probation of good conduct instead of sentencing them at once.

compensation to complainant.gloss: The court's power to order the offender to pay compensation to the person who suffered the loss.

power of superintendence.gloss: The High Court's power over all courts subordinate to it - the source of its criminal rules of practice.

fair trial.gloss: The right to life and personal liberty, read to guarantee a fair and reasonably speedy trial.

legislative competence.gloss: The distribution of law-making power between Parliament and the State legislatures.

complainant.gloss: The payee or holder in due course of the dishonoured cheque - the only person who can set a s.138 case going, by filing the complaint.

accused.gloss: The drawer of the cheque, prosecuted for the dishonour; where the drawer is a company, the company and every person in charge of and responsible to it.

power-of-attorney holder.gloss: A duly authorised agent who, being personally aware of the transaction, may file the complaint and depose for the complainant - a point settled for s.138 by the Supreme Court.

advocate.gloss: The enrolled legal practitioner who appears for the complainant or the accused; the right to appear flows from the Advocates Act.

magistrate.gloss: The Judicial Magistrate of the First Class who takes cognizance of the complaint, tries it summarily and passes judgment.

witness.gloss: A person who gives evidence on the facts; in a s.138 case the complainant's evidence may be led on affidavit.
